Thanks for looping me in. Quick explanation and recommended steps: we've seen this twice in the last quarter. Root causes we've observed:
- Some Calendly embeds pick up the browser timezone of the person who created the event (our rep) when a link is pre-populated or forwarded, which can flip the timezone on the generated invite.
- Mobile bookings can be especially inconsistent because the device locale and calendar sync behave differently across platforms.

Workarounds we use now:
1) Manual .ics — create the meeting in the customer's timezone in Google Calendar, set event timezone explicitly to the customer's zone (e.g., Asia/Singapore), export the .ics and send it. That reliably imports correctly on the recipient side.
2) Use our Chili Piper flow for APAC campaigns — CPM has a more explicit timezone selection in the booking widget and a server-side TZ payload, reducing client-side mismatch.
3) If we must use Calendly, include a short explicit line in the confirmation email: "This event will occur at 09:00 SGT (UTC+8). If your calendar shows a different time, please use this manual invite instead."

For this thread I recommend Rachel picks the confirmed slot and we send an .ics. Jordan — confirm which of Rachel's options works and we'll push the manual invite immediately.
